scope: Present-day cathedral exterior. Include the plaza frontage, north clock and bell tower, the nave and side aisles, and the attached sacristy and chapel. Preserve the open court where supported by the plan.

imageryScreen.firstConsulted: The existing Qualla gallery and its linked native originals.

omitted.reason: The repository label gives an anonymous photograph and an asserted 1901 date with no verifiable publication for this exact image.

The native bytes match the Qualla file, but the precise postcard edition and imprint are unresolved. A contemporary Maier card identified by a Honduran postcard researcher bears a similar name and depicts a different church.

selected.publication: Harper’s New Monthly Magazine, volume 19, number 113, October 1859, printed page 603.
selected.article: A Visit to the Guajiquero Indians, attributed to E. G. Squier (1821–1888).
selected.rightsBasis: Original illustrated periodical published in the United States in 1859. The whole-leaf scan reproduces the original print and contains no modern annotation or photographic subject.
selected.use: West and south elevation rhythm, single domed tower, relief, large arched portal, and side-wall openings. Verify the clock and standing features using written restoration evidence. The historic atrium rail and foreground figures belong to the illustration period.

writtenSources.use: Restoration archaeology establishes the west-facing frontage, three naves, north bell and clock tower, chapels and sacristy, and the open Patio de los Naranjos. Use the written account.
Municipal description identifies the standing cathedral, Baroque setting, and its relationship to the town plaza.
The university confirms the building identity, original publication, and interpretation of the three-quarter engraving. Use the written identification.
